main_text.p: ritiam adjiciant animum &c. Hæc autem omnia pertinere ad promotionem posterioris tabulæ: atque ita hoc tantum pertinere ad officium principum, ut sint innocentiæ, modestiæ, honestatis & pacis publicæ protectores ac vindices. ¶. Hæc & similia pertinent ad secundam tabulam. at insulsum est, si quis inde colligat, principes viros tantum juri inter homines dicendo intentos esse debere, neglecta Dei & religionis curâ.† 1. Cor. 6. 4. & seq. juberi, ut fideles controversias suas (politicas) absque civili magistratu privatim dijudicent: ergo multo minus decere pios, ut dependeant à judicio principum in religionis & fidei negocio. ¶. Nihil detrahit apostolus civili jurisdictioni, sed tantum habet rationem sui temporis, quo fieri non potuit, ut coram infidelibus judicibus contenderent fideles, quin variis calumniis essent obnoxii. Itaque monentur Corinthii, tanquam homines litium studiosi, & falsò veram religionem jactantes, ut istiusmodi controversiæ vel semel potius tollantur, vel domestica disceptatione

page.notes: The first word "ritiam" is a fragment at the top of the page and is kept as printed. The paragraph mark ¶ and the dagger † are as printed and are not read with certainty. The italic passages are judged from the scan and may be incomplete. The catchword "tione" completes "discepta-" from the last line. The left strip shows the neighbouring page and is excluded.
